description: No evidence was found of a CBCG statistical database, SDMX endpoint, open-data API or per-series query interface. All statistical releases observed are distributed as ZIP archives of spreadsheets or as PDFs, published section by section.

result.result_summary: Searched the statistics portal (sr and en) and all its subsections; every dataset link encountered was a .zip or .pdf. No 'baza podataka' / 'data browser' / API affordance surfaced.

why_it_matters: Collection must be file-harvest plus spreadsheet parsing, not API polling. Series identity has to be reconstructed from sheet/column labels, which makes methodology-break detection a manual concern.

description: No standalone CBCG statistical release dedicated to cash usage / currency in circulation / banknote-and-coin turnover was located. Montenegro is unilaterally euroised and does not issue its own currency, so no issuance statistics exist.

result.result_summary: Searches on 'gotovina', 'novčanice i kovanice', 'gotovinski promet' returned reporting-form annexes (denomination templates), the CBCG's own audited financial statements, and payment statistics pages — but no published cash-usage time series.

why_it_matters: Cash-usage intelligence for ME must be inferred indirectly, chiefly from the quarterly cash deposit/withdrawal transaction tables inside the payment services dataset and from ATM withdrawal counts, not from a dedicated series.

description: Two observed discontinuities plus one active delay: national payment traffic indicators were collected on a different basis up to 31.12.2017 (separate legacy archive); the Bilten changed naming and dropped real-sector tables from mid-2025; and the Financial Soundness Indicators page carried a notice that Q1 2026 publication was postponed pending new reporting forms.

result.result_summary: Recorded from the payment-statistics, Bilten and FSI pages directly.

why_it_matters: A naive time-series join across these boundaries would produce false trend conclusions, and an FSI collector must tolerate a missing quarter without treating the source as dead.

description: The cbcg.me site serves the same content under many interchangeable path prefixes (/me/, /en/, /r/, /c/, /public/, and legacy prefixes such as /kursna_lista_arhiva.php/... and /orhanpamuk/...). Search engines surface these variants inconsistently.

result.result_summary: Observed across multiple search result sets returning the same page under different prefixes.

why_it_matters: URL-based deduplication and liveness checks will misfire; a 404 on one prefix is not evidence the source is gone. Canonicalise to the /me/ and /en/ prefixes and re-seed from the sitemap.

description: No URL in this slice is claimed as verified-live. Several were reached only through search-result metadata or a single successful fetch; deep file links (dated ZIPs) will rotate with each release.

result.result_summary: Dated file URLs such as the July 2026 MFI ZIP and the quarterly payment ZIP filename patterns were read off pages and should be re-resolved by parsing the parent page at collection time rather than by constructing filenames.

why_it_matters: Hard-coding dated filenames will silently break the collector each period.

description: The frequently indexed CBCG statistics URL https://www.cbcg.me/r/statistika/statisticki-podaci/platni-promet returned HTTP 404 on fetch, although it appears repeatedly in search results.

result.result_summary: Treated as moved, not dead. The CBCG site serves language/variant path prefixes (/me/, /en/, /r/, /c/, /e/) and appears to have reorganised the statistics tree; the live payment statistics live under /me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/statistika-platnog-prometa/... Crawlers must re-resolve from the statistics index or sitemap rather than pinning deep URLs.

why_it_matters: A collector pinning the old URL would silently lose the payment-traffic series and could wrongly record the source as dead.

description: No dedicated Montenegrin bank-association statistics publication was located. A local-language search for an Udruženje banaka Crne Gore card/ATM/POS statistics series returned only CBCG pages and individual bank sites.

result.result_summary: Either no such association series is published online, or it is not indexed under the terms used. Unlike Serbia or Croatia, Montenegro appears to have no bank-association-level payments statistics layer; CBCG is effectively the sole aggregator.

why_it_matters: Removes a normally productive cross-check on card and terminal counts and concentrates single-source risk on CBCG.

description: No national card switch, domestic card scheme or local processor with published statistics was identified for Montenegro during this cell's searches.

result.result_summary: Assessment literature indicates ATM and POS routing and settlement run through international card scheme networks rather than a domestic switch, which is consistent with the absence of a national scheme statistics publisher.

why_it_matters: Card-level transaction detail beyond the CBCG quarterly aggregates will have to come from international schemes or acquirer disclosures, not from a domestic switch — a structural gap for anyone modelling card economics in ME.

description: The quarterly payment-services and e-money dataset is described as distributed as ZIP archives; the individual archive URLs and their internal file formats were not enumerated in this pass.

result.result_summary: Format and stable-URL pattern unverified. Not recorded as blocked — no access error was observed, only incomplete enumeration.

why_it_matters: Parser design for the richest card/POS/cash dataset in the cell depends on the archive contents; this must be resolved before automation.

description: No open-data API, SDMX endpoint or bulk CSV service was found for CBCG payment statistics; the observed distribution channels are HTML pages, PDFs and ZIP attachments.

result.result_summary: Collection will be scrape-and-parse rather than API-based. Searches in both languages surfaced no data portal for CBCG.

why_it_matters: Raises long-run maintenance cost and fragility of the payments feed, and makes the release calendar essential for scheduling.

description: The IPS (instant payment) system went live only on 20 July 2026, with a first-month figure of 56,678 transactions worth EUR 21.53 million.

result.result_summary: The instant-payments series exists but has almost no history, and it is unclear whether IPS will be reported as a permanent third column in the monthly release or only in ad hoc statements.

why_it_matters: Instant-payment uptake is the highest-value forward-looking series in this cell but is not yet a stable, back-fillable time series; early monitoring of the release structure is needed to avoid a broken schema later.

description: No standalone annual payment-system oversight report was found; CBCG states oversight results are published inside the general annual work report.

result.result_summary: Oversight content is embedded rather than separately published, so it must be extracted from a large multi-topic PDF.

why_it_matters: Oversight narrative (incidents, availability, designated systems) is harder to track and easier to miss than in jurisdictions with a dedicated oversight report.

description: No Montenegrin media outlet was found that maintains a structured, recurring data product (dashboard, downloadable table, standing series page) on cards/ATMs/POS. Every local-media figure encountered was embedded in prose inside a one-off article.

result.result_summary: Searches across bankar.me, cdm.me, rtcg.me, mina.news, gradski.me returned only narrative articles; no media-run dataset or data-journalism section surfaced.

why_it_matters: Collection for this cell must be NLP/figure-extraction over article text, not table scraping; expect high extraction cost and mandatory reconciliation against CBCG.

description: The daily 'Dan' did not appear in any search result set despite being explicitly named in the coverage cell; its site was not returned even on a domain-scoped query.

result.result_summary: Query '"cdm.me" ekonomija OR "dan.co.me" ekonomija ...' returned only cdm.me results. dan.co.me is recorded from prior knowledge, not from an observed result, and is flagged unverified.

why_it_matters: Dan's URL and its economy-section path must be confirmed by the deterministic liveness pass before any crawler is pointed at it; a wrong domain would silently produce zero coverage of one of the three national dailies.

description: Exact economy-section paths for vijesti.me and pobjeda.me were not surfaced by search; only the site roots and third-party ownership profiles were returned.

result.result_summary: Neither a vijesti.me/ekonomija nor a pobjeda.me/ekonomija URL appeared in any result; searches surfaced Croatian/Bosnian outlets and Media Ownership Monitor profiles instead.

why_it_matters: Seed URLs for the two most important dailies are at root level only, so the collector needs a discovery step (sitemap or on-site navigation) rather than a hard-coded section path.

description: Serbian/Montenegrin payment vocabulary is shared with Croatia, Serbia and Bosnia, so local-language queries pull in HNB, tportal, hrportfolio.hr, biznis.ba and Serbian portals.

result.result_summary: The 'kartično plaćanje gotovina' query returned mostly Croatian and Bosnian outlets plus ECB pages, with only one genuinely Montenegrin hit (rtcg.me, inflacija.me).

why_it_matters: Any automated sr-language collection for this cell must be domain-restricted to .me (plus known ME outlets) or it will be dominated by regional noise and produce cross-country contamination of Montenegrin figures.

description: Specific card/cash volumes for 2025 (81.5m card transactions, ~EUR 2bn value, 5.5m cash transactions) were seen in a single local outlet's article summary and are not independently confirmed here.

result.result_summary: Single-source figure from gradski.me summarising an apparent CBCG-derived dataset; the underlying CBCG release was not located in this run.

why_it_matters: Illustrates the core risk of this cell — media figures are second-hand, sometimes rounded or misattributed, and must be reconciled with cbcg.me before entering any analysis.

description: No paywall, archive-pricing or licensing page was located for any of the Montenegrin outlets in this cell.

result.result_summary: Access and legal status for vijesti.me, pobjeda.me, dan.co.me, mina.news were inferred, not observed; robots.txt and ToS were not inspected in this run.

why_it_matters: Legal/access fields for most candidates in this slice are hypotheses; a compliance check is required before any systematic crawl, especially for the MINA agency wire.

description: No EBRD project or technical-assistance operation dedicated specifically to Montenegro payment-systems modernisation was found. EBRD's Montenegro financial-sector activity surfaced as SME credit lines, guarantees, 'Go Digital in the Western Balkans' and financial-stability advisory rather than a payments-infrastructure project.

result.result_summary: Searches returned SME/green/digital finance operations only; the payments-infrastructure role in Montenegro is carried by Banca d'Italia/ECB (TIPS clone) and EPC (SEPA), not EBRD.

why_it_matters: Avoids over-weighting EBRD as a payments-data source for ME; collection effort should be redirected to EPC, ECB/Banca d'Italia, WBIF and the EC Reform Agenda.

description: The only located World Bank/IMF FSAP payment-and-settlement-system technical note for Montenegro dates from the 2015 FSAP update (published Jan 2016). No newer FSAP financial-infrastructure note for Montenegro was found.

result.result_summary: FSAP payments assessment is ~10 years old and predates PSD2 transposition, SEPA accession and TIPS clone.

why_it_matters: The richest independent payments-infrastructure diagnostic is stale; current benchmarking must lean on EC reports, EPC and ECB/Banca d'Italia material instead.

description: No Montenegrin/Serbian-language EBRD, World Bank or IMF diagnostic on Montenegro's payments market was located; IFI assessment material for this cell exists in English only, while local-language coverage of the same events comes from CBCG, gov.me and media rather than the assessing institutions.

result.result_summary: Local-language searches surfaced government and media coverage (bankar.me, slobodnaevropa.org, eu.me, cbcg.me) but no IFI assessment translations.

why_it_matters: Local-language collection for this cell should target CBCG/gov.me/Skupstina primary documents, not translated IFI reports which do not appear to exist.

description: No EU/donor source was found that publishes Montenegro-specific card, ATM/POS or cash-usage statistics as a structured dataset. ECB payments statistics (SDW/Data Portal) cover EU/EEA reporting agents; Montenegro is not an ECB reporting country despite euroisation.

result.result_summary: Cell yields narrative and milestone data, plus institution-level SEPA adherence counts, but not time-series card/ATM/POS statistics.

why_it_matters: Card/ATM/POS series for ME must be sourced from CBCG's own payment statistics (a different cell), not from EU/IFI publishers.

description: Montenegrin government documents are served from wapi.gov.me under opaque UUID download URLs with no discoverable index, so systematic enumeration of Chapter 4 working-group reports and negotiating positions is not possible by crawling alone.

result.result_summary: Only individually search-surfaced PDFs were reachable.

why_it_matters: Collection design must use search-engine harvesting or the eu.me portal as the entry point rather than a site crawl.

description: No CBCG working paper (Radna studija) specifically about payment systems, card usage, POS/ATM networks or cash demand was identified in the visible series index.

result.result_summary: The Radne studije index lists inflation, climate, public debt, tourism, real estate, FDI, credit/deposit and COVID-banking topics; the fetched page exposed titles and PDF links but no authors/years, and nothing payments-specific surfaced.

why_it_matters: The cell's highest-value hypothesis — that CBCG researchers publish payment-behaviour analysis outside statistical releases — is not confirmed; A4 payment analysis may instead live in the Financial Stability Report or Godišnji izvještaj rather than the working-paper series.

description: No published Faculty of Economics Podgorica study on cashless payment / card adoption was found via local-language search.

result.result_summary: Serbian-language query 'Ekonomski fakultet Podgorica istraživanje bezgotovinsko plaćanje kartice' returned only institutional pages (ucg.ac.me/ef, programme lists, social media) and no research output.

why_it_matters: Suggests domestic academic payment research is either unindexed, published in Serbian-language journals off the open web, or embedded in theses — requiring repository sweeps rather than search-engine discovery.

description: No Montenegro-specific article from the Montenegrin Journal of Economics on payments/cards/digital adoption was surfaced in this run.

result.result_summary: The journal itself was confirmed (mnje.com, ISSN 1800-6698/1800-5845, ELIT Podgorica) but the search returned only non-Montenegrin digital-payments literature.

why_it_matters: Article-level discovery for this journal needs the DOAJ/Scopus index or the journal archive rather than general web search; do not conclude the journal lacks relevant papers.

description: Domestic commercial survey work (DeFacto, CEED, Ipsos Adria) appears to be client-confidential with no public report library.

result.result_summary: Company profiles and directory entries were found, but no downloadable banking/payments studies.

why_it_matters: Merchant/consumer survey evidence for ME likely exists but is only reachable via press releases or direct commercial contact — collection method must be relationship-based, not scraping.

description: No page in this slice was fetched-and-confirmed beyond the CBCG working-paper index; all other URLs come from search-result metadata.

result.result_summary: Only https://www.cbcg.me/me/publikacije/ostale-publikacije/radne-studije was retrieved directly; the rest are unverified candidate URLs.

why_it_matters: Liveness must be established by the deterministic verification pass; confidence scores here reflect provenance quality, not reachability.

description: No dedicated Montenegrin consumer price/fee COMPARISON site (independent of the regulator) for cards, ATM withdrawal or POS/merchant service fees was found - no ME equivalent of a kamatica/kamate-style comparison portal surfaced in local-language search.

result.result_summary: Only the CBCG statutory comparison tables and occasional bankar.me fee journalism cover this need; no independent comparison aggregator identified.

why_it_matters: Merchant-side pricing (MSC/MDR, terminal rental) therefore has no public comparison channel in ME; pricing intelligence must come from bank tariff PDFs one by one, which is a heavier collection design.

description: The seed acronym 'CRPS' does not correspond to the Montenegrin procurement portal. In ME, CRPS historically denotes the Central Register of Business Entities (Centralni registar privrednih subjekata, now under the Tax Administration / Privredni sud), while the procurement system is CeJN (Centralni elektronski javne nabavke) at cejn.gov.me, with ujn.gov.me as the policy directorate.

result.result_summary: Searches on 'CRPS ... javne nabavke' returned the company register and unrelated Serbian/Bosnian portals rather than ME tenders.

why_it_matters: A collector keyed on 'CRPS' would miss the actual tender source entirely; the glossary must separate CRPS (company register - itself a useful actor-map source) from CeJN (procurement).

description: Local-language queries for ME procurement and job ads repeatedly return Serbian and Bosnian sources (jnportal.ujn.gov.rs, ejn.gov.ba, addiko.rs), because the language is shared.

result.result_summary: Roughly half of the top results for 'portal javnih nabavki' / 'oglas za posao ... banka' were RS or BA rather than ME.

why_it_matters: Any automated sr-language collector needs a hard country filter (.me domain, 'Crna Gora', ME city names) or it will silently ingest Serbian market data as Montenegrin.

description: The official ME procurement portal cejn.gov.me/tenders is a client-side rendered application; a plain HTTP fetch returned only the string 'CeJN' with no notices, search form or documented API.

result.result_summary: Content not retrievable by simple fetch. This is a hypothesis of JS-rendering, not evidence the site is dead - it must be re-tested with a headless browser and by inspecting XHR endpoints.

why_it_matters: The single most important source in this cell needs a browser-based or API-based collector, not an HTML scraper; budget for that in collection design.

description: No published ME tender or award specifically for ATMs (bankomati), POS terminals or card processing was located within this run's searches - only a generic mention of thermal rolls for cash registers/POS terminals in aggregator descriptions, which was not confirmed on an official notice.

result.result_summary: Category existence is plausible but unproven; keyword search inside the portal (not via general web search) is required.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's premise that ME ATM/POS demand is largely invisible to open web search and must be reached by in-portal CPV/keyword querying plus indirect channels.

description: No ME-specific national payments/cards industry AWARD programme (e.g. a domestic 'best card product' or 'best ATM network' award) was identified; awards touching ME banks are international titles (Global Finance, Euromoney, The Banker) reported second-hand by local media.

result.result_summary: Awards channel for ME is thin and foreign-issued.

why_it_matters: Awards will contribute little independent signal for this market; deprioritise relative to tenders, job ads and regulator fee tables.

description: cbcg.me serves the same page under several locale prefixes (/me/, /en/, /r/, /c/, /reg/, /eng/). Two fetches using the /r/ prefix (the /r/ payment-services-and-e-money page and /r/statistika/statisticki-podaci/platni-promet) returned HTTP 404, while the /me/ and /en/ equivalents rendered fine.

result.result_summary: 404 on /r/ variants; content retrieved successfully from /me/ and /en/ paths. Treated as a routing quirk, not a dead source.

why_it_matters: A collector keyed to search-engine-supplied /r/ or /c/ URLs will silently fail; canonicalise every CBCG URL to /me/ (sr) and /en/ before scheduling.

description: No open data API, SDMX endpoint or CSV service was found for the CBCG card/ATM/POS statistics. The quarterly series is distributed only as per-table ZIP archives (Excel inside) under /slike_i_fajlovi/fajlovi/fajlovi_platni_promet/usluge_e-novac/{year}/.

result.result_summary: Only ZIP/Excel and PDF distribution observed.

why_it_matters: Collection must be a file-harvest plus spreadsheet parser, with a schema-drift check each quarter; filename conventions embed the quarter and are the only reliable versioning signal.

description: No source was found publishing a contactless-vs-e-commerce split of Montenegrin card transactions as a standalone series. The CBCG breakdown found is by terminal type ('po vrsti terminala', i.e. ATM vs POS vs other) and by domestic/cross-border, not by acceptance mode. A World Bank assessment separately notes that active card counts are not published.

result.result_summary: Terminal-type and geography splits exist; contactless / remote (CNP) split not located; active-card counts not published.

why_it_matters: The contactless and e-commerce share requested in this cell may have to be inferred from card-scheme or bank statements rather than official statistics — a material caveat for any adoption claim.

description: Local-language searching surfaced no Montenegrin equivalent of a national card-scheme/processor statistics publication (no local ATM-sharing network bulletin comparable to BH mreža in Bosnia was confirmed for Montenegro).

result.result_summary: Searches in sr returned only CBCG, UBCG and bank pages; no domestic scheme/processor statistics publisher identified.

why_it_matters: Switch/processor-level volume data, if it exists, is likely private and would need commercial or interview-based access.

description: No standalone CBCG cash-operations report exists. Searches in Serbian for 'izvještaj o poslovima sa gotovinom' returned only the generic Izvještaj o radu CBCG, the audited financial statements and unrelated supervisory reporting decisions — no dedicated cash/vault report analogous to the cash reports issued by issuing central banks.

result.result_summary: Cash-operations narrative appears to be embedded as a section inside the Annual Work Report rather than published separately; not yet verified inside a PDF.

why_it_matters: Any pipeline expecting a discrete 'cash report' document for Montenegro will find nothing; the collector must PDF-mine the Annual Work Report instead.

description: Because Montenegro uses the euro unilaterally and does not issue it, no national currency-in-circulation statistic is published by CBCG. CBCG's own euroisation page states it cannot control the money supply and that euro quantity in circulation depends on ECB policy and external flows.

result.result_summary: CiC for Montenegro exists only as an estimate — the clearest one located is an IMF technical assistance estimate built from historical CiC data for a seigniorage-loss calculation.

why_it_matters: The headline metric a cash-cycle analyst would normally anchor on does not exist as an official series; estimates and their methodology must be sourced and caveated.

description: The CBCG English payment-system statistics page exposes only RTGS/DNS indicator ZIPs and a historical national payment transactions ZIP frozen at 31.12.2017; it lists no ATM/POS or cash-withdrawal dataset. The ATM/POS and cash withdrawal data are instead on the Montenegrin-language 'Podaci o platnim uslugama i elektronskom novcu' page under key functions, not under Statistics.

result.result_summary: English-only navigation would have missed the ATM/POS and cash-withdrawal series entirely; the Serbian-language route found them.

why_it_matters: Concrete demonstration that English-only discovery under-covers Montenegro, and a warning that the collector must target the platni-promet path, not the statistika path.

description: No Montenegrin equivalent of the ECB SPACE study or a national payment-diary/cash-usage survey was located. MONSTAT's Household Budget Survey publishes expenditure structure (food 37.1%, housing/utilities 15.1% in the 2021 wave, 1,333 households) but the published outputs contain no payment-instrument or cash-share variable.

result.result_summary: Searched in Serbian with 'gotovinsko plaćanje' and 'anketa o potrošnji domaćinstava'; no cash-share-of-payments survey surfaced.

why_it_matters: Cash-usage share at point of sale for Montenegro cannot be sourced directly and must be proxied from ATM withdrawal volumes vs card POS turnover in the CBCG quarterly datasets.

description: Searches in Serbian for an Association of Banks of Montenegro ('Udruženje banaka Crne Gore') bulletin with ATM/card statistics returned only CBCG pages and a Serbian banking-association journal article; no live Montenegrin bank-association statistics publication was identified.

result.result_summary: No confirmed URL for a Montenegrin bank association cash/ATM bulletin. Treated as unconfirmed, not as non-existent.

why_it_matters: In neighbouring markets the bank association is a key aggregator; its absence or invisibility in Montenegro concentrates dependence on CBCG as effectively the sole aggregator.

description: Euronet is publicly described as operating an Independent ATM Deployment network including Montenegro, but no source was found that attributes Montenegro's ATM estate by operator, and no Montenegro-specific Euronet ATM count was located in the press releases retrieved.

result.result_summary: IAD presence is credible but unquantified; CBCG acceptance-device counts are unattributed totals.

why_it_matters: Independent deployers and bank-owned ATMs imply very different cash-handling procurement channels; the split is currently unobservable from public data.

description: Searched in Montenegrin for a Ministry of Finance monthly macroeconomic bulletin analogous to Serbia's 'Bilten javnih finansija'. No such standing monthly bulletin surfaced for Montenegro; search results were dominated by the Croatian and Serbian finance ministries. What the Montenegrin ministry does publish appears to be monthly budget-execution reports, quarterly/annual public-debt reports and the Economic Reform Programme.

result.result_summary: No Montenegrin MoF 'makroekonomski bilten' identified; the cell's fiscal cadence rests on budget-execution and debt reports instead.

why_it_matters: The seed query assumed a bulletin that may not exist under that name; collection design should target the ministry's document library by document type rather than waiting for a named bulletin.

description: No public statistical output was found from the electronic fiscalization system (in force since 2021) breaking transactions down by payment method — i.e. no official cash-versus-cashless invoice counts or values published by the Revenue and Customs Administration. All located material is vendor guidance and compliance how-tos (Telekom, Pošta Crne Gore, ERP vendors), not statistics.

result.result_summary: Fiscalization payment-method aggregates appear to exist as data but not as publications.

why_it_matters: This is the single richest potential cash-usage dataset in Montenegro and it is currently dark to open collection; a free-access-to-information request is the realistic route and should be planned deliberately.

description: No evidence surfaced of a PxWeb-style interactive statistical database or public API at MONSTAT; dissemination appears to be page.php HTML index pages linking PDF and XLSX files under /uploads/files/ and the legacy /userfiles/file/ paths.

result.result_summary: MONSTAT looks document-oriented rather than database-oriented; no API confirmed.

why_it_matters: Collection cost is materially higher (PDF/XLSX parsing, two legacy path conventions) and Eurostat's Montenegro series become the preferred machine-readable channel where coverage overlaps.

description: MONSTAT page ids are not stable across the cg/ and eng/ trees or over time: the id=475 page resolved to construction activity (2012 archive) in English while local-language results associate 475 with retail trade, and file assets are split between the legacy /userfiles/file/ and current /uploads/files/ roots.

result.result_summary: Numeric page ids and asset paths are unreliable long-term identifiers.

why_it_matters: A collector keyed on page ids will silently drift onto the wrong domain; keying on the saopštenje/novosti archive index and on release titles is safer.

description: No Montenegrin-language official statistical term was found for POS-terminal or ATM counts within MONSTAT's own domain vocabulary (searches surfaced only central-bank material, which is outside this cell). MONSTAT appears not to publish acceptance-infrastructure statistics at all.

result.result_summary: Acceptance-network counts are absent from the statistical-office estate.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's role is denominators only; the numerators (POS/ATM/card counts) must come from the central-bank cell, and any attempt to source them here will waste collection effort.

description: BIS CPMI Red Book payments statistics do not cover Montenegro. Searches of the CPMI member/jurisdiction lists (27 member jurisdictions, expanded in 2018 to add Argentina, Indonesia, Spain) returned no Montenegro entry.

result.result_summary: Montenegro is not a CPMI member jurisdiction; no ME series should be expected in the Red Book / data.bis.org CPMI topic datasets. BIS remains valuable only as a definitional standard and comparator set.

why_it_matters: Prevents wasted collection effort and stops a false assumption in the run scope that BIS is a Montenegro data source.

description: ECB does not collect euro-substitution / euroisation survey data for Montenegro because the euro is legal tender there (same for Kosovo). ECB euro-substitution ratios exist for North Macedonia and Serbia but not ME.

result.result_summary: No ECB euro-cash-substitution series for Montenegro; ECB coverage of ME is qualitative (cooperation programme, occasional papers), not a statistical series.

why_it_matters: Cash-usage analysis for Montenegro cannot lean on ECB euroisation statistics and must come from CBCG or IMF FAS-type indicators instead.

description: IMF FAS POS-terminal series for Montenegro was not directly confirmed in the search layer; FAS documentation describes POS terminals as introduced via a pilot study with rural/urban disaggregation, and ATM-per-100k values for ME were visible, but the POS-per-100k ME series itself was not observed.

result.result_summary: ATM density for ME appears present in FAS/WDI; POS density presence in FAS for ME is a hypothesis requiring a direct dataset query.

why_it_matters: POS density is a core deliverable of this cell; the collection pass must explicitly test for the ME POS series rather than assume it.

description: Whether the Central Bank of Montenegro responded to the World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey (6th round, Oct 2023) was not established from search results.

result.result_summary: GPSS is a strong candidate but ME participation is unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: If CBCG did not respond, GPSS yields nothing for ME and priority should drop.

description: Local-language (sr/me/bs) searching surfaced very little supranational statistical material: IMF publishes some country reports in Bosnian/Serbian (e.g. the Bosnian-language BiH country report and older Bosnian Article IV translations), but no Montenegro-specific IMF/World Bank/Eurostat statistical dataset in Montenegrin was found. Local-language coverage is dominated by media reporting (Dan, MINA, Investitor, Bankar.me) and by CBCG/MONSTAT pages describing the relationship rather than by the supranational data itself.

result.result_summary: Supranational statistical databases covering ME are effectively English-only; local-language value is limited to intermediary/commentary layers.

why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations: the sr-language search budget for this cell is better spent on national publishers (cell scope elsewhere) than on chasing translated international datasets.

description: IMF's data portal has been re-platformed: legacy links use query strings (data.imf.org/?sk=E5DCAB7E-...) while newer links use path form (data.imf.org/en/datasets/IMF.STA:FAS). Both forms appear live in search results; neither was fetch-verified in this pass.

result.result_summary: URL form for IMF datasets is in flux; the deterministic verification pass should test both forms.

why_it_matters: Hard-coding a single IMF URL form risks silent collection failure.

description: Searched in Serbian/Montenegrin for a UBCG statistical bulletin ('bilten', 'statistički pregled', 'sektorski podaci'). Every 'bilten' hit for Montenegrin banking resolves to the Central Bank's Bilten CBCG, not to the association.

result.result_summary: No evidence that UBCG publishes its own periodic statistical bulletin with member-aggregated card/ATM/POS data; its recurring publications are the Bankar magazine, the annual work programme and the annual activity review.

why_it_matters: Analysts should not expect association-sourced aggregates to substitute for CBCG payment statistics in Montenegro; the association's statistical value is mainly in magazine articles and conference decks.

description: The site menu advertises a PUBLIKACIJE section at https://ubcg.info/publikacije/ but the fetch returned HTTP 404. A guessed archive path https://ubcg.info/casopis-bankar/ also returned 404.

result.result_summary: Publications are in practice reachable only as individual dated posts (e.g. /2026/02/13/bankar-br-72/) and as direct wp-content/uploads PDF URLs. Treat the 404 as a moved/renamed page, not as a dead source.

why_it_matters: A collector keyed on /publikacije/ would silently collect nothing; the harvester must instead walk monthly archives and the uploads directory.

description: The association is commonly assumed to sit on 'ubcg.me'; searches confirm the live property is ubcg.info (with /en/ mirror). The acronym UBCG also collides with 'Udruženje bibliotekara Crne Gore' (librarians) at ubcgc.ac.me.

result.result_summary: Noisy acronym — queries on 'UBCG' alone return librarian-association and University of Montenegro bulletin results.

why_it_matters: Query design must pair 'UBCG' with 'banaka'/'banking' to avoid a polluted crawl frontier.

description: Searched in Serbian for a Montenegrin microfinance-institutions association, a leasing association and a card/payment-scheme industry body.

result.result_summary: No such standalone associations surfaced; non-bank financial institutions appear to be covered either by CBCG supervision pages or by the Chamber of Economy's combined banking/finance/insurance board.

why_it_matters: Sector self-reporting outside banks proper is thin in Montenegro — the aggregation function sits with CBCG and, secondarily, with the Chamber board.

description: The 2024 activity review PDF fetched as a largely image-based document with little extractable text.

result.result_summary: Association PDFs may require OCR; content was not readable through plain text extraction.

why_it_matters: Any pipeline over UBCG PDFs needs an OCR stage or the annual reports will be silently empty.

description: Searches in Montenegrin for investor presentations by ME banks ('prezentacija za investitore', 'investor presentation') surfaced no bank-level investor decks. Montenegrin banks are unlisted or thinly listed and do not produce IR presentation decks the way listed CEE banks do.

result.result_summary: No ME-bank investor presentation found in this pass; only annual reports, audited statements and bond prospectuses exist as disclosure formats.

why_it_matters: The cell brief anticipated investor presentations as a KPI source; collection design should instead centre on annual reports + prospectuses + tariffs.

description: No annual-report or reports index page was located in this pass for Ziraat Bank Montenegro, Universal Capital Bank or Zapad banka on their own domains; only CBCG-hosted balance sheets and third-party aggregator profiles were found.

result.result_summary: Tail banks appear to disclose only via the regulator, not their own sites.

why_it_matters: Entity-level card/ATM/POS data for the tail of the market may be structurally unavailable; the CBCG-hosted filings become the only route.

description: WebFetch of https://www.ckb.me/... failed with 'unable to verify the first certificate'. This is a TLS chain/client issue, and the domain returns live content in search indexing.

result.result_summary: CKB pages recorded as unverified, not dead.

why_it_matters: A naive liveness pass could wrongly mark the market leader's disclosure hub as dead; the deterministic verifier should use a tolerant TLS chain or headless browser for ckb.me.

description: No bank published a machine-readable series of POS terminals installed or acquired volume; the only entity-level POS figure found was a marketing claim on CKB's corporate page (>4,000 terminals).

result.result_summary: POS estate data is narrative/marketing, not tabular.

why_it_matters: Bottom-up POS market sizing for Montenegro will need triangulation across marketing claims, tariff documents and locator scrapes rather than reported statistics.

description: The CBCG Register of E-money Institutions was fetched directly and states, in Montenegrin, that no e-money institution is currently entered ('U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac').

result.result_summary: Zero licensed domestic e-money issuers in Montenegro at time of scouting. Any Montenegrin 'e-wallet' proposition therefore operates under a payment-institution licence, a bank, or a foreign passport — not a domestic e-money licence.

why_it_matters: Removes an entire expected source family from the cell. Analysts must not infer e-money volumes from a register that has no members, and the CBCG e-money statistics tables will be structurally sparse for domestic issuers.

description: Two entities in the CBCG payment-institution register — 'Business integration and business intelligence d.o.o. Podgorica' and 'Capital Transfer MNE d.o.o. Podgorica' — could not be matched to a confirmed corporate website in either Montenegrin or English search.

result.result_summary: Capital Transfer MNE appears only as a name in aggregator and secondary text; the BIBI entity produced no usable web presence at all. Their register PDFs on cbcg.me remain the only located primary evidence.

why_it_matters: Two of seven licensees are effectively invisible outside the register, so licensee counts overstate the number of observable, quantifiable actors. Their volumes must be reached via CRPS financial statements rather than own publications.

description: No source was found in which Montenegrin payment institutions publish their own transaction volumes or values. Searches in Montenegrin for licensee names combined with volume terms returned marketing pages, hiring notices and press interviews only.

result.result_summary: Licensee 'own published volumes' — a premise of this cell's brief — largely do not exist as public disclosures in Montenegro. Coverage, tariffs, service catalogues and location counts are published; transaction counts are not.

why_it_matters: Non-bank payment flow sizing must be built from the CBCG aggregate quarterly payment-services statistics and from CRPS-filed financial statements, not from licensee self-reporting. Setting this expectation early prevents a fruitless collection stream.

description: Secondary sources disagree on the ownership of Montenegro Transfers d.o.o. Podgorica: one attributes it to the Alta group (alongside Alta Pay Podgorica), another states Eki Transfers holds 100%.

result.result_summary: Ownership unresolved from open web sources; both claims are secondary and neither was corroborated against a primary filing in this run.

why_it_matters: Group structure determines whether Montenegro's two largest remittance agents are independent competitors or one economic actor — a material distinction for concentration analysis. Must be settled against CRPS before publication.

description: No established Montenegrin-language term or public register was located for crypto-asset service providers / VASPs operating as payment-adjacent actors; searches around fintech licensing surfaced only payment-institution and e-money categories.

result.result_summary: No MiCA-equivalent Montenegrin register or licensee list found in this run.

why_it_matters: If crypto on/off-ramps are in scope for the payments landscape, this cell currently has no local-language vocabulary or pointer source for them, and the gap is unmeasured rather than empty.

description: The CBCG sub-page specifically holding 'Finansijski izvještaji platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac' was referenced in search snippets but its exact URL was not confirmed by direct fetch; the supervision-section landing page was recorded instead with reduced confidence.

result.result_summary: Firm-level financial reports for payment institutions are believed published by CBCG, exact location unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: This is potentially the single best firm-level quantitative source in the cell. It should be located by crawling the supervision section tree before concluding it does not exist.

description: No Visa press release or study specific to Montenegro (contactless milestone, cardholder spend, tourism spend) was located, in either English or Serbian. Visa's ME presence surfaces only as a country landing page under visasoutheasteurope.com and as part of CEMEA/SEE-wide commentary.

result.result_summary: Searches in en and sr returned tourism/visa-policy noise plus generic Visa corporate content; no ME-specific Visa data release found.

why_it_matters: Visa is one of the two schemes expected to publish ME market milestones; if it genuinely does not publish country data for ME, Mastercard's MasterIndex becomes a single-source dependency for scheme-side demand data, which is a concentration risk for workstream A4.

description: The term 'Visa' is severely polluted in the Montenegrin context by immigration/visa-policy content ('visa requirements', 'viza za Crnu Goru', visa-free travel suspensions), which dominates both en and sr result sets.

result.result_summary: Multiple queries containing 'Visa Montenegro' returned travel-visa results almost exclusively.

why_it_matters: Any automated collection pipeline must disambiguate the card scheme from travel visas, e.g. by pairing with 'kartica', 'platna', 'beskontaktno', 'acquiring', or restricting to visa.com/visasoutheasteurope.com domains. Without this the Visa channel is effectively unsearchable.

description: No AllSecure announcement (saopštenje) about Montenegro was found on AllSecure's own domains; its ME footprint is evidenced only indirectly, through merchant checkout boilerplate naming 'AllSecure d.o.o. u saradnji sa Hipotekarnom bankom'.

result.result_summary: Local-language query 'AllSecure Crna Gora platni promet e-commerce banka saopštenje' returned CBCG and bank pages, not vendor PR.

why_it_matters: It means the gateway/acquirer map for ME e-commerce must be assembled bottom-up from merchant disclosures rather than top-down from vendor press — a slower but more complete method that should be built into the collection design.

description: No ATM hardware vendor (NCR/NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf/Wincor Nixdorf, Nautilus Hyosung) customer page, case study, or delivery announcement naming a Montenegrin bank was found in either language.

result.result_summary: The sr query on bankomati + vendor names returned only spare-parts resellers and generic vendor pages; no ME customer references.

why_it_matters: The ATM-hardware supplier layer for ME appears to be intermediated entirely through Payten/ASEE as regional distributor and service provider, meaning the ATM fleet composition must be inferred from Payten/ASEE disclosures and from bank ATM locators, not from the OEMs.

description: No Montenegro-specific Halcom entity, client-bank list, or announcement was found; all located Halcom material is Serbian, Bosnian or Slovenian.

result.result_summary: Query in sr returned NLB Komercijalna (RS), ASA Banka (BA) and Halcom RS/SI resources only.

why_it_matters: Halcom may have no material Montenegrin footprint, in which case the corporate e-banking layer in ME is supplied by other vendors (candidate: Asseco/Payten, in-house). This is an open actor-map question, not a settled negative.

description: No published count of MoneyGet ATMs in Montenegro was found; Payten publishes group-level figures (approx. 9,500 ATMs, 600,000 POS across 16 countries, ~150 POS/ATM service clients) and a Serbia-specific 100-location milestone, but no ME breakdown.

result.result_summary: Group aggregates found; ME-specific counts absent from vendor PR.

why_it_matters: Fleet size for ME must be derived by counting the moneyget.me ATM locator rather than read off a published number — a method decision that must be made explicit so the derived figure is never mistaken for a vendor-published statistic.
